question.problem:
Consider two sets of $25$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{25},$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{25}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\sum }_{i=1}^{25}{x}_{i}=250,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{25}{y}_{i}=265, \\  & {\sum }_{i=1}^{25}{x}_{i}^{2}=3\,460,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{25}{y}_{i}^{2}=5\,720.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the sum of the squared deviations from the mean for the points ${x}_{i}.$

${S}_{xx}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the sum of squared deviations from the mean for the data ${x}_{i}$ can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}-\frac{1}{n}{({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given statistics in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & =3\,460-\frac{1}{25}(250)^{2} \\  & =3\,460-2\,500 \\  & =960.\end{aligned}
$$
